# Demo docs — generated by Docloom's production parser

These two files are **unmodified output** of Docloom's `buildApiMarkdown`,
run over public GitHub repos (AI descriptions would normally fill the
description column; the structural facts are exactly what shipping users
get):

- [`dub-api.md`](./dub-api.md) — 57 endpoints from [dub](https://github.com/steven-tey/dub) (file cap: 50 of 520 route files)
- [`calcom-api.md`](./calcom-api.md) — 42 endpoints from [cal.com](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com)

## Measured results (parser-eval, Sep 2026)

| Repo | Routes parsed | Request bodies detected | Bodies fully resolved | Routes with response shapes | Query/header inputs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dub | 79 (of 520 files, capped at 50) | 11 | 9 (+3 after cross-file resolution) | 45 (53 shapes) | 4 routes, 5 inputs |
| cal.com | 42 | 4 | 3 | 33 (86 shapes, 32 fully resolved) | 14 routes, 20 inputs |

Note the honest-gap behavior throughout: fields the parser can't prove
say **"not documented in source"** instead of being invented — including
per-response-branch fields like `error` above, where two 400 branches
differ in whether `error` is a plain string.

## Reproduce

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/steven-tey/dub /tmp/dub
node scripts/parser-eval.mjs /tmp/dub
node scripts/generate-demo-docs.mjs /tmp/dub steven-tey/dub main demo/dub-api.md
```

No DB, no network, no API keys — the parser and markdown builder are pure.
